name: Refugee Status (Asylum Regulation Act 2014)

requirements.blocker_text: Registered with Sudan's refugee-administering Commission and holds valid refugee identity documentation.

Must obtain permission before leaving a designated place of residence -- refugee status in Sudan is administered under an encampment-style residence-restriction model, not a general freedom-of-movement model.

outcome.duration_length: not defined by the source material located in this build

sources.title: UNHCR Rights Mapping and Analysis Platform (RIMAP) -- Sudan's Asylum Regulation Act 2014: recognized refugees receive national treatment for public relief/assistance, elementary education, court access, and religious freedom; favorable (better-than-ordinary-alien) treatment for housing, self-employment, movement, and post-elementary education; refugees must respect Sudanese law, obtain permission before leaving their designated place of residence, and carry valid refugee identification -- eligibility criteria and the initial application process were not detailed in the excerpt retrieved

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Sudan). STATUS: DRAFT -- tier-2 UNHCR-hosted summary is the clearest source located; no tier-1 Sudanese-government-hosted copy of the Asylum Regulation Act 2014 was located in this build, and even the tier-2 source did not detail the actual eligibility criteria or application process for INITIAL recognition -- only post-recognition rights and obligations, a genuine and disclosed sourcing gap. STRUCTURAL FINDING, WORTH CONTRASTING AGAINST UGANDA'S REFUGEE MODEL BUILT EARLIER IN THIS DATASET: Sudan's framework requires refugees to obtain permission before leaving their designated place of residence -- an encampment-style restriction on freedom of movement, structurally opposite to Uganda's open-border, non-camp, land-allocation model. THE OVERWHELMING PRACTICAL REALITY, STATED PLAINLY: as of this build, Sudan is described by UN and humanitarian sources as the site of the world's LARGEST displacement crisis -- but this is now overwhelmingly a story of Sudan PRODUCING refugees and internally displaced persons (fleeing the SAF-RSF civil war into Chad, Egypt, South Sudan, and elsewhere, and displaced within Sudan itself) rather than Sudan functioning as a stable HOST country under this 2014 Act, even though Sudan has historically hosted significant refugee populations from South Sudan, Eritrea, and Ethiopia. This dataset models the inbound legal framework as it exists on paper; whether the Commission administering it is currently functioning in any given part of the country amid active conflict is a separate, unresolved question this build does not attempt to answer.
